transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. How can I help you today?

Hello, Doctor. Thank you so much for fitting me in. I hope I'm not taking up time from people who are, you know, truly unwell. 

I’m mostly doing alright, but... well, I suppose I should just be honest. I feel a bit silly even saying this out loud, and I really hope you don't think poorly of me, but... what actually scared me enough to come in today is that I’ve started having these... thoughts. Nothing drastic, I promise! I absolutely don't have any sort of plan to harm myself, I would never do that. But I just keep catching myself thinking things like... well, like it would just be simpler if I didn’t wake up tomorrow. 

I'm sorry, I know that sounds awful. Is that... is that the sort of thing it's appropriate to talk about here?
How often have these thoughts been happening, and have they been going on for a specific amount of time?

Oh, well, they certainly aren't happening all the time, I promise. Just... occasionally, when things feel a bit overwhelming. I'd say it's been going on for... oh, about eight months now? Yes, roughly eight months. 

It started right around the time my brother’s health and... well, his behavior... changed so suddenly. It's just been quite an adjustment, and I suppose I haven't been handling the stress of it as gracefully as I should have. I feel terrible even complaining about it, really, since he's the one who is unwell. 

I hope that’s the kind of information you were looking for? I want to make sure I'm answering your questions properly.
In the past week, how often have these thoughts come up, and have they felt more intense or more frequent than before?

Oh, well... in the past week... I suppose they might have popped up just a tiny bit more often. Maybe... a few times? But please don't be alarmed! They really aren't intense at all. It's just that same fleeting thought, like I mentioned before... just a quiet little sigh of, 'Oh, wouldn't it be so much easier to just not wake up tomorrow?' 

But as soon as the thought comes, I brush it right away! I really do. I know it's a terrible way to think, and I'd never, ever act on it. I don't have any sort of plan or anything dreadful like that. It's just... a momentary weakness, I suppose, when I'm feeling a bit tired. 

I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is. Does that make sense? I just want to be completely transparent with you, even if it's a bit embarrassing to admit.
Have you noticed yourself losing interest or taking less pleasure in activities that you used to enjoy, like hobbies, work, or spending time with loved ones?

Oh, well... I suppose a little bit, yes. I hope that doesn't make me sound lazy or ungrateful for the free time I have now. I know I should be making the most of it. 

I used to just love painting—watercolors, mostly. I still try to keep up with it, I really do! I'll set out all my brushes and my paints, just like I always have. But... lately, I'll just sit there staring at the blank paper, and eventually, I just end up putting it all away again. It's silly, but... the pleasure I used to feel in capturing the color and the light... it just doesn’t seem to arrive anymore. 

I still try to keep busy with other things, though! I don't just sit around all day. But I suppose the joy just isn't quite there right now. Is it normal to lose interest in things like that when you're stressed? I hope I'm not making a fuss over nothing.
Have you noticed feeling down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, or do your low moods come and go more sporadically?

Oh, goodness... well, I suppose it’s more of an everyday sort of feeling lately. I really try not to let it show, and I do hope I haven't been bringing anyone down with it. 

It’s just... most days, I feel as if this sort of... gray film has settled over everything. Even when I’m doing perfectly lovely things, like making a cup of tea or just looking out at my garden—which is usually such a joy—there’s just this quiet heaviness inside me. I keep trying to reason my way out of it, to tell myself I have no right to feel this way, but it just sort of lingers there. 

I do try to keep a smile on, though, I promise! I just haven't quite been able to shake this low feeling. I hope that’s alright to admit? I don't want to sound like I'm just feeling sorry for myself.
Have you noticed that even small tasks, like getting dressed or making a meal, are taking much more effort lately, or that you're feeling unusually tired most of the time?

Oh... well, I suppose... maybe just a tiny bit? I really don't want to sound like I'm complaining about everyday chores. I know everyone gets a little tired sometimes, especially at my age, right? 

I do manage to get everything done, I promise! I still make my meals and keep myself tidy. It's just... lately, getting up to do those things feels like... like I have to push through a bit of molasses to get started. Just a little extra effort to convince myself to get dressed or put the kettle on. 

But once I'm up and doing it, it's fine! I really am trying my best to keep on top of things. I hope it doesn't seem like I'm letting myself go. Do you think it's normal to feel just a little worn out like that?
Have you noticed yourself thinking or moving more slowly than usual lately, like your thoughts are sluggish or your body feels weighed down?

Oh, goodness, no... I don't believe so. I mean, I certainly hope I haven't seemed sluggish to you today! I try very hard to keep my wits about me. I still do my morning crosswords and read quite a bit, so my thoughts feel perfectly clear, thankfully. 

And as for moving slowly... well, maybe just the usual little stiffness you get at sixty-eight, but certainly nothing out of the ordinary! I still get around just fine once I'm on my feet. That's a good sign, isn't it? I really do try to stay as sharp and active as I can, so I hope I'm doing all the right things there.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight recently? For example, have you been eating significantly less or lost weight without trying?

Oh, dear... well, I don't think so. I really do try to make sure I eat properly, you know. I certainly wouldn't want to cause any worry by skipping meals or anything like that. 

I suppose my appetite is... well, perfectly normal, really. I still have my regular meals, and I make sure to sit down and eat them properly. I haven't noticed my clothes fitting any differently, so my weight must be staying quite steady. 

I know how important it is to keep one's strength up, especially at my age, so I do make a point of eating. That's the right thing to do, isn't it? I hope I'm taking good care of myself in that regard.
Have you noticed a loss of energy or felt unusually fatigued, even when you haven't been doing much physically taxing?

Oh... no, I really wouldn't say that. I know I mentioned earlier that it takes a little extra push to get started on things sometimes, but... my actual energy is quite good, really! 

I certainly don't just sit in my chair feeling exhausted all day, I promise you that. Once I'm up, I have plenty of energy to get through my day. I make sure to keep myself occupied with my reading and my little routines around the house. I think it's so important not to just give in to feeling tired, don't you agree? 

So, no, I haven't had any unusual fatigue like that... I hope that shows I'm keeping myself up and about properly?
Have you found that you no longer enjoy almost any activities, not just painting, but even things you’ve always found pleasurable, like reading or spending time with family?

Oh, goodness, I... well, I certainly try to keep up with everything. I really do! I wouldn't want you to think I'm just sitting around doing nothing all day. 

I still enjoy my family, of course—I mean, I'm always happy to see them, even if I'm perhaps a little quieter than usual. And reading is still... well, it's a good way to pass the time. 

But with my painting... I suppose I have been struggling just a tiny bit there. I still set out all my watercolor things on the table sometimes, just like I always have. I want to do it, I really do! But then I'll just sit there, staring at the blank paper, and... I end up putting it all away again. It’s silly, I know, but that feeling I used to get—the joy of seeing the colors and the light come together—it just doesn't seem to arrive right now. 

But I'm still trying! I haven't given up on it completely. I hope that's the right attitude to have? I just wouldn't want you to think I've stopped trying to enjoy things.
Have you found yourself feeling more guilty or like you're a burden to others, even when there's no real reason for it?

Oh, goodness, a burden? No, I certainly try my very best not to be a burden to anyone. I always make sure to handle my own affairs and keep out of people's way so my family doesn't have to worry about me. I think it's so important to be self-sufficient and helpful, don't you? 

But... as for feeling guilty... well. I suppose... I hesitate to even mention it, because I know it's probably not very rational of me, and I wouldn't want you to think I'm just sitting around feeling sorry for myself. But I do have these moments where I... I keep going back over my brother’s decline. 

I just can't seem to help telling myself that if I had only been a better sister, or... or just a bit more attentive to him, I would have noticed what was happening sooner. I keep thinking I could have prevented some of it, if I'd just been sharper. 

It's silly to dwell on things in the past, I know. I really do try to push those thoughts away and stay positive. I know I shouldn't let my mind wander to such unhelpful places... that's the right way to handle it, isn't it? I promise I am trying my best to focus on the present.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep lately, like having trouble falling asleep, waking up too early, or sleeping much more than usual?

Oh, my sleep... well, I really try to keep a good schedule, I do. I make sure to go to bed at a reasonable hour, because I know how important rest is for keeping up with everything. I wouldn't want to be sleeping the day away! 

But... I suppose my nights haven't been perfectly smooth lately. It's just a little uneven when I first try to drift off. And then... well, sometimes I find myself waking up quite early, around three or four in the morning. 

I try to just go right back to sleep, of course. But my mind just starts buzzing a bit... thinking about all those little things, you know? Like whether I filled out those forms correctly, or if I handled certain phone calls the right way. Just silly little worries that I know I shouldn't be fretting over at that hour. 

I really do try to quiet my thoughts, but by the time morning comes, I sometimes feel like I haven't rested as much as I should have. I hope that doesn't sound like I'm complaining too much? I know everyone has a bad night now and then, and I'm sure I just need to try a little harder to relax before bed. That's the best way to handle it, right?
